Priya: The reworked 52 line saves riders eight minutes each way. That is why it deserves the priority lane.
Tomas: Eight minutes is the schedule fantasy. On paper the old line saved six. Riders care about the door-to-door reality.
Priya: We both want the fastest reliable trip. The question is just what the new routing actually delivers.
Tomas: Agreed. Give me measured run times from the first month, not modeled ones, and I will back the lane either way.

extraction.mainQuestion: Does the reworked 52 line actually save riders about eight minutes per trip?

positions.label: Grant the priority lane now
positions.thesis: The reworked 52 deserves the priority lane because it saves riders about eight minutes each way.
positions.steelman: If realized savings match the schedule, delaying the lane just forfeits rider time the route has already earned.

groundingQuotes.quote: The reworked 52 line saves riders eight minutes each way.
That is why it deserves the priority lane.

positions.label: Decide on measured data
positions.thesis: The priority lane decision should wait for measured door-to-door run times rather than rely on modeled schedules.
positions.steelman: Modeled schedules have overstated this corridor before, and infrastructure decisions should track realized performance.

groundingQuotes.quote: Give me measured run times from the first month, not modeled ones, and I will back the lane either way.

claims.statement: The reworked 52 saves riders about eight minutes each way in practice.

resolution.condition: One month of measured door-to-door run times compared against the pre-change baseline.

resolution.condition: Compare scheduled versus measured run times across the last several route changes.
